extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and applicants preparing/responding to Office Actions
extracted.subtask_description: Standardized USPTO form paragraphs and procedural guidance for examining patent applications, addressing submission/file-format requirements for electronic media and statutory bases for rejections under 35 U.S.C. (e.g., §101, §102, §115). Used to draft objections, rejections, and required corrections in Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification lacking incorporation-by-reference statement for compact disc/text file (EFS-Web)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application contains compact disc(s) or text file(s) submitted via EFS-Web as part of the originally filed subject matter but does not contain an incorporation-by-reference statement for those discs/files, the specification must be amended to include an appropriate incorporation-by-reference statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite 37 CFR 1.77(b)(5) and MPEP § 502.05; applicant is required to insert the incorporation-by-reference statement in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table column/row relationship must be maintained in ASCII text files
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables submitted as ASCII text files (via EFS-Web or on compact disc) must maintain the spatial orientation of the cell entries so that data remain properly aligned within rows and columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If table data are misaligned, applicant must submit a replacement text file via EFS-Web or on compact disc with properly aligned table data. See 37 CFR 1.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data files on CD-ROM/CD-R must be in ASCII file format
rubrics_metrics.description: A data file (table, computer program listing, Sequence Listing) submitted on CD-ROM/CD-R must be in ASCII format; proprietary or non-ASCII formats are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmit file(s) in ASCII format; no new matter may be introduced when converting to ASCII. See 37 CFR 1.52(e). Examiner notes: indicate file name and whether it is a proprietary non-ASCII file or contains non-ASCII characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables under 51 pages cannot be submitted only as ASCII text file
rubrics_metrics.description: A description table consisting of fewer than 51 pages may not be submitted only as an ASCII text file as part of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must cancel references to the table in text format in the specification, file a paper version of the table in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52 or file a PDF via EFS-Web, and change all appropriate references in the specification. See MPEP § 608.05(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing >300 lines must be appendix in text format
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer program listing of more than 300 lines included in the specification must instead be submitted as an appendix in text format (via EFS-Web or on compact disc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with 37 CFR 1.96(c); the appendix must be referenced appropriately in the specification (see 37 CFR 1.77(b)(5)). Applicant must cancel the current listing in the specification, file the listing appendix as a text file, and insert an appropriate reference at the beginning of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing of >60 and ≤300 lines placement
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer program listing contained in the written specification of more than 60 lines and no more than 300 lines must be positioned at the end of the specification and before the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, incorporate the listing in a text file submitted via EFS-Web or on compact disc in compliance with 37 CFR 1.96, or insert the listing after the detailed description but before the claims. Cancel the in-specification printout if using an electronic submission. See 37 CFR 1.96(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must list compact disc(s) and associated files (amendments with CDs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment is filed that includes compact disc(s), the paper portion of the specification must identify each disc and list all files contained on the disc, including file name, file size, and file creation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend the specification to identify each disc and the files on each disc. See 37 CFR 1.52(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Microfiche appendix unacceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer program listing filed as a 'microfiche appendix' is unacceptable and does not conform to current requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A computer program listing must conform to the requirements of 37 CFR 1.96; use this paragraph if a microfiche appendix was filed after March 1, 2001 or if an earlier microfiche appendix is non-compliant. Insert the date the microfiche was filed in the form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: CD-ROM/CD-R amendment must state if two CDs are identical
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment involves multiple compact discs, the transmittal letter must include a statement that the two compact discs are identical (if they are).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the transmittal letter lacks the required statement that the discs are identical, correction is required. Cite 37 CFR 1.52(e)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal letter must list CD machine format, OS compatibility, files, sizes, dates
rubrics_metrics.description: A transmittal letter submitted with an amendment that contains compact disc(s) must identify each disc and provide: the machine format, operating system compatibility, a list of files with names, sizes in bytes, dates of creation, and any other special information necessary to identify, maintain, and interpret the information on the compact disc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the transmittal letter does not include this listing, require the applicant to provide it. See 37 CFR 1.52(e)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must include incorporation-by-reference for amended/added CDs or text files
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment amends or adds compact discs or text files submitted via EFS-Web, the specification must be updated to include an appropriate incorporation-by-reference statement for those newly added or amended files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.77(b)(5) and 1.52(e)(5). Use when amendment includes CD/text file but required incorporation-by-reference statement is missing or not updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two submitted CDs must be identical (if claimed identical)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two compact discs submitted as part of an amendment are not identical but the submission purports them to be identical, an objection is raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Object under 37 CFR 1.52(e)(4) if discs are not identical. See also form paragraph for missing statement in transmittal letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data file submitted with amendment on CD-ROM/CD-R must be ASCII
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment contains a data file on CD-ROM/CD-R that is not in ASCII, the applicant must resubmit the file(s) in ASCII format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new matter may be introduced when converting to ASCII. Use this whenever a data file (table, program listing, Sequence Listing) is submitted in a non-ASCII file format. Indicate file name and whether it is proprietary or contains non-ASCII characters. See 37 CFR 1.52(e)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: CD-ROM/CD-R unreadable — ISO 9660 and ASCII required
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submitted compact disc is unreadable, the applicant must resubmit the files in International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 9660 standard and ASCII format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmit in ISO 9660 and ASCII as required by 37 CFR 1.52(e)(3); no new matter may be introduced by the resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: CD-ROM/CD-R contains viruses — objection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submitted compact disc contains at least one virus, the amendment is objected to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require correction; use the form paragraph indicating the disc contains viruses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement compact disc must include all files (amendment completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A replacement compact disc provided to effect an amendment must include all of the files that were on the original disc (both amended and unamended) to be a complete replacement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If replacement disc omits unamended files, object because amendments to a compact disc can only be made by providing a complete replacement disc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure incomprehensible — 37 CFR 1.71 (precludes reasonable search)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the disclosure is so incomprehensible that a reasonable search of the prior art cannot be made by the examiner, the disclosure is objected to under 37 CFR 1.71 and the applicant must clarify the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must submit an amendment to clarify the disclosure without introducing new matter. Indicate page numbers and features not understood. Use this when a search cannot be made. See related paragraphs for improper idiomatic English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unconventional terminology preventing examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application uses terminology so different from art-accepted terminology that a proper search cannot be made, the applicant must clarify terminology or correlate with art-accepted terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clarifications or correlations; be careful not to introduce new matter. Indicate the problematic terminology and affected pages/features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application subject to AIA First Inventor to File provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application was filed on or after March 16, 2013, it is examined under the AIA first inventor to file provisions; use the appropriate AIA form paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph in any application subject to the first inventor-to-file provisions of the AIA. Precede certain other form paragraphs with this where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of statutory basis — 35 U.S.C. 101 and improper inventorship (35 U.S.C.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph quoting 35 U.S.C. 101 and 35 U.S.C.115(a) when the application sets forth incorrect inventorship; claims may be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 and 35 U.S.C. 115 for failing to set forth correct inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert bracketed explanation of incorrect inventorship; precede rejections under 35 U.S.C. 101 with this paragraph in first actions on merits and final rejections. Use 7.04.02.aia where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 — nonstatutory (not within four statutory categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 101 when the claimed invention does not fall within at least one of the four statutory categories (process, machine, manufacture, composition of matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the bracketed explanation, identify what the claim(s) are directed to and explain why it does not fall within one of the four categories (e.g., signal per se, mere information as data, contract, human being). Precede with form paragraph 7.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 — judicial exception without significantly more
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject claims that are directed to a judicial exception (law of nature, natural phenomenon, abstract idea) that lack 'significantly more' to transform the exception into patent-eligible subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the judicial exception, explain why the claim is directed to it, and identify additional elements and why they do not amount to significantly more (considered separately and in combination). Provide examples: products of nature must be markedly different (e.g., DNA must be markedly different), generic computer implementation is insufficient, routine data-gathering steps do not add meaningful limitations. Use form paragraph 7.05.015 and related MPEP §2106 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 — utility lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 101 when the claimed invention lacks patentable utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear explanation of lack of utility (bracketed). See MPEP §§ 706.03(a) and 2105–2107.03 for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 — inoperative
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject claims when the disclosed invention is inoperative and therefore lacks utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give explanation in bracketed text as to why the invention is inoperative. See MPEP for examples and related utility guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility rejections under 35 U.S.C. 101 and enablement under 35 U.S.C. 112(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim may be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 for lack of utility and also under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph) if the specification does not support an asserted or well-established utility such that one skilled in the art would know how to use the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where enablement is at issue, apply In re Wands (858 F.2d 731) factors and provide undue experimentation analysis (see MPEP §§2164–2164.08(c)). Use appropriate form paragraphs to explain the lack of asserted/well-established utility and reasons for enablement deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate claims objection (37 CFR 1.75)
rubrics_metrics.description: When two claims are duplicates or so close that they cover the same thing (despite slight wording differences), object to the duplicate claim under 37 CFR 1.75 as a substantial duplicate of an allowed claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one claim is allowable, object to the other as a substantial duplicate. Use form paragraph 7.05.05 (warning) or 7.05.06 (objection) as appropriate. If duplicate claims are not allowable, use the objection paragraph. Insert claim numbers and explanations in brackets as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formats for utility/credibility findings (Format A/B/C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use different format templates depending on whether an asserted utility is absent, not specific and substantial, not credible, or multiple utilities have varying credibility/specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format A: use when no asserted utility or asserted utility not specific and substantial; Format B: use when asserted utility not credible; Format C: use when multiple utilities exist and none are specific, substantial, and credible. Insert claim numbers and tailored explanations per form paragraph 7.05.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice when prior art applicable under both pre-AIA and AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: When a prior art rejection is made and the determination whether the application is subject to AIA or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103 might be incorrect, correction of the statutory basis later will not be treated as a new ground of rejection if the prior art and rationale supporting the rejection are the same under either status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph in Office Actions where a prior art rejection is made in applications with actual filing dates on or after March 16, 2013, that claim priority to applications filed before March 16, 2013. Use only once per Office Action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim limitation that relates to a tax strategy deemed prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim limitation that has been interpreted as a tax strategy for reducing, avoiding, or deferring tax liability is treated as within the prior art and insufficient to differentiate the claimed invention from the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recite the claim limitation and identify affected claim numbers in the form paragraph. See MPEP §2124.01 for more information. Use when a limitation reads on a tax strategy (AIA Section 14 implications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of statutory basis — 35 U.S.C. 102 (AIA) (form paragraph usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph providing the quotation/text of the AIA-amended 35 U.S.C. 102 to serve as the statutory basis for rejections under that section in an Office Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph where appropriate; in first actions on the merits and final rejections this paragraph must precede certain rejections. Form paragraphs 7.07.aia, 7.08.aia, 7.12.aia and 7.14.aia are to be used only once in a given Office Action. Precede by 7.03.aia where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of statutory basis — pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 (form paragraph usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph quoting the appropriate pre-AIA statutory language of 35 U.S.C. 102 to serve as the basis for pre-AIA prior art rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 7.07.fti where pre-AIA 102 is the statutory basis. Precede with other indicated paragraphs (e.g., 7.07.fti must precede certain other pre-AIA paragraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 102(b) — activity more than one year prior to filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pre-AIA 102(b), the invention was patented or described in a printed publication, in public use, or on sale more than one year prior to the U.S. filing date, making the invention unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.09.fti, preceded by 7.07.fti (and possibly 7.08.fti). Insert relevant dates and explain the activity more than one year prior to filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 102(c) — invention abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pre-AIA 102(c), an invention that has been abandoned is not entitled to a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.10.fti, preceded by 7.07.fti and optionally 7.08.fti/7.09.fti as needed. Provide the factual basis for abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 102(d) — foreign patenting before US application
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pre-AIA 102(d), the invention was first patented or the subject of an inventor's certificate in a foreign country prior to the U.S. filing date or within statutory time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.11.fti as appropriate and provide relevant foreign patenting dates/facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 102(a)(1) — activity before the effective filing date (published/available to public)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under AIA 102(a)(1), the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.08.aia in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 where AIA 102/103 examination applies. Precede by 7.03.aia and 7.07.aia as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 102(a)(2) — prior US patent/application publication/wipo publication naming another inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Under AIA 102(a)(2), the claimed invention was described in a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO published application that names another inventor and has an effectively filed date earlier than the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.12.aia when such references exist; understand interplay with AIA and how effectively filed dates apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 102(a) — activity by another before applicant's invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pre-AIA 102(a), the invention was known or used by others in this country, or patented/described in a printed publication in this or a foreign country, before the invention by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.08.fti for applicable situations (with required preceding paragraphs 7.03.aia and 7.07.aia where relevant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 102(e) — earlier-filed U.S. patent/application by another (AIPA/AIPA/2002 amendments considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), the invention was described in an earlier-filed U.S. patent or patent application publication by another (including certain international applications treated as U.S. filings under statutory conditions), providing a prior art date for the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.12.fti when the reference is a U.S. patent or publication filed under specific conditions (see enumerated subpoints). Carefully consider benefit/priority claims (119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), 386(c)) and the international filing date conditions (e.g., PCT filing date after Nov 29, 2000). See accompanying examiner notes for conditions and precedences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIPA special case — 102(e) reference from PCT filed prior to Nov 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: Special handling is required when the reference is a U.S. patent issued from, or a publication of, an international application (PCT) having an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000; certain pre-AIPA 102(e) rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.12.01.fti for references that are U.S. patents issued directly/indirectly from a national stage of, or continuing application claiming benefit to, an international application with an international filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000. See the detailed examiner notes for when to apply.
